title: The Iberian Pact
summary: Salazar and the Spanish ambassador Nicolás Franco — the victor’s brother — signed the Treaty of Friendship and Non-Aggression in Lisbon on 17 March 1939, a fortnight before the Spanish Civil War formally ended and with its outcome already settled; it was ratified on the 25th. The two states recognised each other’s frontiers, undertook not to help an aggressor against the other, and bound themselves to consult before acting. What three years of support for the Nationalist side had been for was substantially this: a Spain with no claim on Portugal and no intention of letting anybody else cross it. An additional protocol signed in Lisbon in July 1940 reaffirmed peninsular neutrality once the war had begun, and the arrangement held through the years when Spanish sympathies ran to the Axis and Portuguese ones to Britain. It is in the atlas because Portuguese neutrality in the Second World War, and everything Salazar was later able to trade on it, rested here.

actors.role: the regime whose foreign policy it set
